newsitem.title: CANADA: Grandma Lee's shares rise on new strategy.
newsitem.headline: Grandma Lee's shares rise on new strategy.

text.p: Shares in Grandma Lee's Inc almost doubled on Thursday from Monday's opening price after the restaurant chain operator announced a new strategy and a new name, Heritage Concepts International Inc.

The stock gained four cents to 0.22 in heavy mid-afternoon turnover of 1.1 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It was up sharply from 0.125 at the start of the week in heights it has not seen since November 20, 1997.
Jerry Janik, the chief executive brought from Churchill Heights Properties Ltd in a friendly takeover last year, said that "people are buying into the vision that we enunciated the other day."

Janik said on Monday that the company planned to expand its restaurant outlets and bring aboard new concepts, including a chain of bars patterned after the one featured in the television show, "Cheers".

It also plans to seek new financing through mortgaging one of properties, Janik said. "By mid-summer, GLI/Heritage will have no bank debt, assets totaling C$8 million with only C$3 million in mortgages, cash flows from current operations and from the acquired business well as money in the bank."
With those expansions Grandma Lee's will post its first real profitable quarter soon, he said.
